summary: Iteration 6 backend-only test for Phase 3 Shopping List 'both' purchase_price_type (PPT) extension. Result: 40/40 PASS (13 new + 27 regression). Validated all 6 scoped behaviors: (1) POST /api/inventory/shopping-list with body {text, qty, purchase_price_type:'both', purchase_price:4.5} returns 201 and item.purchase_price_type=='both'; both 'regular' and 'deal' still accepted as regressions. (2) POST with product_id of a product whose PPT='both' and NO purchase_price_type in payload now inherits 'both' VERBATIM — previous coercion to regular/deal is fixed (server.py:1319-1320). Explicit payload PPT still wins over product PPT. Sanity: regular product still inherits 'regular'. (3) PATCH /api/inventory/shopping-list/{id} with {purchase_price_type:'both'} returns 200 and item.purchase_price_type=='both'. (4) POST /api/inventory/stock/submit with a product configured (avg_sales.quantity=10/period_days=5 -> per_day=2, max_inventory_days=7, PPT='both') and on-hand set to 0 via /api/inventory/stock/set, creates a NEW continuous-list entry with purchase_price_type=='both' and quantity==14.0 (server.py:1473,1486). (5) Regression smoke: POST/GET/DELETE /api/inventory/shopping-lists; GET /api/inventory/shopping-list; GET suppliers/categories/products endpoints — all 200. Full prior phase 5 suite (27 tests) re-run green. (6) Invalid PPT 'super-deal' returns 422 on both POST and PATCH (Literal validation enforced).
action_items: No backend blockers. Phase 3 'both' PPT extension is verified end-to-end across create/patch/inherit/submit paths. Main agent may proceed with frontend integration (e.g., expose 'both' in the PPT picker in Shopping List screens and product form).

Reminder (carried over from iter 5): server.py is now ~1637 lines (was ~1401), still well past the 700-line split threshold. Consider splitting into routers/{stores,auth,users,checklists,accounting,inventory,chat}.py — non-blocker but tech debt continues to accumulate.
critical_code_review_comments: ShoppingListItemCreate.purchase_price_type (server.py:1250) and ShoppingListItemUpdate.purchase_price_type (server.py:1260) are Optional[Literal['regular','deal','both']]. Pydantic correctly rejects unknown values with 422 — verified.

create_shopping_item (server.py:1313-1320) sets `purchase_price_type = payload.purchase_price_type` and ONLY falls back to product's PPT (verbatim, including 'both') when payload omits it AND a product_id is provided. The earlier coercion to {regular,deal} has been removed — verified by test_inherits_both_when_not_provided. The product fallback `p.get('purchase_price_type', 'regular')` is safe for legacy products without the field.

submit_stock (server.py:1465,1473,1486): suggestions include the product's PPT verbatim; line 1473 has a defensive `if s['purchase_price_type'] in ('regular','deal','both') else 'regular'` guard — belt-and-suspenders since Pydantic already enforces this at create/update time. New-insert branch (line 1486) writes ppt verbatim — verified 'both' is preserved by test_submit_creates_continuous_entry_with_both.

submit_stock existing-entry branch (server.py:1478) uses `existing.get('purchase_price_type') or ppt`. This means an existing entry's PPT is preserved on re-submit; only when existing.PPT is None/empty does the product's current PPT take over. Acceptable semantics (user edits stick) but worth being aware of: if user creates a manual entry with PPT='regular' for a product whose PPT later changes to 'both', the existing entry will NOT be auto-upgraded. Not a bug per spec, just documented.
ShoppingListItem (server.py:1275): the inline comment still says `# 'regular' | 'deal' | None` — outdated, should read `'regular' | 'deal' | 'both' | None`. Cosmetic only, no functional impact.
MongoDB _id is consistently excluded across all reads (verified via response shape in all 13 new tests).
Backend supervisor reloaded cleanly after the change (no startup errors in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log); all endpoints respond 200/201/204/422 as expected.
